title: Grateful Dead Live at Red Rocks Amphitheatre on 1982-07-29
lineage: FOB - Senn 421's> Sony TC-D5 (at mouth of the stage)> Nak Dragon Playback> HHB CDR-850 (no DAT gen)> CDR

ai_review.summary: An excellent audience recording of the rain‑soaked Red Rocks show, featuring a smoking Crazy Fingers, thunderous Cold Rain > Samson and a monster Other One.
ai_review.review: The crowd‑sourced tape captured by Jim Wise delivers crystal‑clear ambience with deep bass and minimal drop‑outs, making it one of the best audience recordings from the 1982 Red Rocks run. Musically the night is a high‑energy masterpiece – the second set erupts with Cold Rain > Samson, an incendiary Crazy Fingers, a soaring Miracle and a rain‑drenched Other One that many fans call legendary. Jerry’s lead work is on fire, Phil builds a massive ramp into The Other One, and Brent’s vocals add extra sparkle despite occasional mix quirks.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently glowing remarks about both performance (standout songs, high energy) and recording quality (crisp, well‑balanced audience tape); only minor mix complaints keep it just shy of perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Listeners praise the deep bass, clear mids and overall balance; a few note excess chatter and occasional over‑bearing Bobby rhythm guitar but no major drop‑outs or muffling.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set starts slow and spacey, building momentum with Stranger; second set launches into high‑octane Cold Rain > Samson followed by Crazy Fingers, Miracle and an epic Other One, ending with a powerful encore.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar tone is described as "smoking" and "beautiful", especially on Crazy Fingers and the solo sections of Cold Rain > Samson.
band_member_comments.Phil: Praised for a perfect bass ramp into The Other One, delivering a powerful crescendo.
band_member_comments.Bob: Some listeners note his rhythm guitar can be overwhelming in the mix, but his vocal contributions are appreciated.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent’s keyboards and vocals receive mixed comments – praised for adding sparkle yet occasionally low in the mix.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming is highlighted as high‑energy, especially during the Samson transition and the drum break before The Other One.
